metadata.title: KBC Void / Hubble Bubble as Large-Scale Assembly Index Anomaly

phenomenon.name: KBC Void (Keenan-Barger-Cowie Void)
phenomenon.description: A ~1 billion light-year radius region of 20-50% underdensity relative to cosmic mean, with Earth/Local Group positioned near its center. Challenges the cosmological principle of large-scale homogeneity.

discovery_timeline.event: Keenan, Barger, Cowie identify local underdensity via galaxy counts
Siewert et al. confirm BAO distortion consistent with void
Banik et al. (RAS NAM): BAO data fits void model 100 million times better

key_references.title: Evidence for a ~300 Mpc Scale Underdensity in the Local Galaxy Distribution
Kinematic Cosmological Dipoles from the 2M++ Galaxy Redshift Compilation

indicators: Local expansion rate (H₀) diverges from global CMB prediction by ~8-11%

technical_risks.risk: KBC Void may be observational artifact (systematic errors in galaxy counts)
technical_risks.mitigation: Multi-survey validation (2M++, CF2, DESI, LSST when available)

technical_risks.risk: TNG simulations may not resolve void physics at required scale
technical_risks.mitigation: Supplement with AbacusSummit or Millennium-XXL for large volumes

technical_risks.risk: SNN void detection accuracy insufficient for cosmological inference
technical_risks.mitigation: Hybrid approach: SNN seeding + traditional watershed algorithm refinement

scientific_risks.risk: Void explanation of Hubble tension incomplete (needs additional new physics)
scientific_risks.mitigation: A_c framework designed for partial anomalies; flag as 'pre-transition' rather than solved
scientific_risks.impact: Low (still valid as anomaly detection case)

scientific_risks.mitigation: Independent replication by external group; publish methodology openly
